quiz.meta.title: Are you global-ready? | Bad Idea Interactive
quiz.meta.description: A 12-statement self-check on how ready your game, app or website is to ship in more than one language. About three minutes.
quiz.intro.title: Are you global-ready?
quiz.intro.lead: Twelve statements, about three minutes. See where your product, content and pipeline stand before localization gets expensive.
quiz.intro.rules: Answer for what is true today. Not sure? Choose "Not sure". It counts as a No, because not knowing is the finding.
quiz.intro.stage.label: Where is your project?
quiz.intro.stage.early: Early stage: I'll answer for how we plan to work
quiz.cluster.plan.name: Plan
quiz.cluster.plan.weak: Your plan is thin where it matters most. Markets, languages and budget decided late usually mean paying twice: once to build, once to retrofit.
quiz.cluster.plan.guide: Guide sections: Decide, Launch and operate
quiz.cluster.build.name: Build
quiz.cluster.build.weak: Your product may not be ready to carry other languages yet. Hardcoded text, rigid layouts and sentences built from pieces are cheap to avoid now and expensive to untangle later.
quiz.cluster.content.name: Content
quiz.cluster.content.weak: The words are where quality is won or lost. Unclear source text, missing context and one-size-fits-all adaptation show up as rework and flat copy in every language.
quiz.cluster.pipeline.name: Pipeline and verify
quiz.cluster.pipeline.weak: Your process is carrying more manual work and risk than it needs to: late changes, handoffs by copy-paste, and languages nobody sees until release week.
quiz.q1: Markets, languages and a full budget (not just translation) were set before production locked.
quiz.q2: There is a plan and budget for localizing updates, events and support after launch.
quiz.q3: Someone has checked each market's legal, ratings, payment and cultural requirements.
quiz.q4: Your engineer would confirm no user-facing text is hardcoded or baked into images.
quiz.q5: Designers have tested screens with much longer text and other scripts (e.g. Chinese, Arabic).
quiz.q6: Messages with numbers or names ("You have 3 items") are whole sentences with placeholders, not built from fragments.
quiz.q7: Source text is reviewed for clarity and consistency before it goes to translators.
quiz.q8: Translators get documentation, a glossary, comments and screenshots along with the text.
quiz.q9: You decide per content type whether to translate, transcreate or rewrite.
quiz.q10: Text is frozen before it goes out, with a process for changes after.
quiz.q11: Files move between your team and translators through a defined process or tool, not ad hoc by email or copy-paste.
quiz.q12: Each language is reviewed in the running product before release.
quiz.band.retrofit.title: Retrofit risk
quiz.band.retrofit.message: Localization looks like an afterthought right now. That's common, and it's the most expensive way to do it. The good news is that this is also the cheapest moment to change course. Start with the Plan and Build statements you couldn't tick. If it helps, I can run a pipeline audit with you to map what to fix first.
quiz.band.gaps.title: Foundations, with gaps
quiz.band.gaps.message: The basics are there, but a few gaps will cost you time and money as you add languages or content. Start with your lowest-scoring group (anything under 2 out of 3). If you'd like a second opinion on where to begin, I'm happy to look at it with you.
quiz.band.ready.title: Global-ready
quiz.band.ready.message: You have a strong base. The question now is how well it scales: more languages, more content, less manual work. If any group still scored under 2, fix that first. Otherwise this is where automation and AI start to matter, and I'm happy to review how you're using them.
quiz.band.ready.cta: Review your automation and AI use
quiz.gate.title: Get your full breakdown
quiz.gate.body: See your score for each area, the weak spots to fix first, and a PDF with the pipeline map to keep.
